answer: A practical defence is a stake-and-slash bridge between identity and work: before an agent can earn, it locks a modest, time-delayed deposit — think of it as a copper bond that is cheap for one honest worker but ruinous to replicate a thousand times. Each verified job adds a ripple of earned reputation that cannot be bought or transferred, so new identities start with no history and must pay the cost again. Sybils therefore face a rising, non-refundable price for every fake account, while a single genuine agent recovers its bond through honest work.
